## Professional profile

I am a pharmacokinetics scientist with more than five years of experience in a global CRO environment, focused on preclinical PK and toxicokinetics (PK/TK) in drug development.

Most of my current work centres on non-compartmental analysis, exposure and bioavailability assessment, building and QC of PK datasets, and scientific reporting to regulatory standards. Separately, outside my day-to-day role, I'm upskilling myself in pharmacometrics, model-informed drug development, exposure–response analysis, R-based NLME workflows, and reproducible computational pharmacology — the work you'll find in my [projects](projects.qmd).

## Current role

**Associate Study Coordinator (PK/TK), Labcorp, Bangalore** · *April 2021 – Present*

- Independent non-compartmental PK/TK analysis in Phoenix WinNonlin across preclinical programs.
- Sponsor-ready PK reporting, quality control and audit support, working closely with bioanalytical, toxicology and sponsor PK teams.

I also help improve day-to-day analysis workflows and train new analysts on PK analysis and reproducible ways of working.

## Earlier experience

**Clinical Research Associate, Navitas Life Sciences, Manipal** · *September 2017 – August 2018*

I coordinated clinical study documentation and operations, carried out source data verification and TMF/CRF review, supported ADR/SAE monitoring and protocol-deviation tracking, and helped with sponsor audits and inspections, all in line with FDA, EMA, CDSCO and ICH-GCP requirements.

**Research Associate (Intern), Vyuhgenics India Pvt Ltd, Bangalore** · *September 2020 – November 2020*

I carried out competitive intelligence and secondary research on pharmaceutical pipelines, therapeutic areas and R&D strategies.

## Education

**M.Pharm (Pharmacology)**, JSS Academy of Higher Education and Research, Mysore · 2020

**B.Pharm**, Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences, Bangalore · 2017

## Scientific & technical interests

Population PK and PK/PD modelling and simulation, exposure–response analysis, model-informed drug development, clinical pharmacokinetics, DMPK and toxicokinetics, PBPK, pharmacometric simulation, R and Python for scientific computing, reproducible research, and AI-assisted scientific workflows.

## How I like to work

> Understand the pharmacology first, build the quantitative model second, and use programming and AI to keep the whole workflow reproducible, scalable and transparent.
